entities.title: Build Cyberspace, the repository in 3D
entities.summary: Eight pull requests took the spec to cyberspace-explorer.com: plumbing, the city, selection, the folder tower, the street, layers and the skyline, finishing and launch, then the records.
entities.goal: Cyberspace works as docs/cyberspace-mode-spec.md says, for every repository the flat page can open, and the spec's acceptance checklist passes.
entities.approach: One pull request per step, into main, in order. Each branches from the latest main, passes CI, updates the .dev files for what it built, and marks its step done here; where a step departs from the spec, the same pull request changes the spec. Merging deploys, so the Flat / Cyberspace switch stayed hidden while the steps were built, when only an address with ~space in it opened Cyberspace; the owner had it shown on 2026-11-15, after step 6 (decision cyberspace-launch). A sub-session builds each step from the spec and the copies of the design in docs/cyberspace-design/, one at a time, because every step changes index.html and builds on the one before. Before the owner merges a step, it is checked: the diff against its section of the spec, the tests and both validators on a clean checkout, the page in a real browser beside the renders, the flat page's regression list and, from step 2, the ?spacestats readout. The budget for 400 parts is measured on a branch, perf/400-parts, that holds a generated .cyberspace-explorer/ tree and is never merged.

steps.title: Correct the spec against the code, copy the design into docs/cyberspace-design/, and record this plan and its open questions

Plumbing: the hidden switch, the ~space address, route() and showSpace, #space, loadThree() pinned to three.js 0.187.0, the WebGL check and every fallback, spaceTheme() and the new tokens, the sky, the ground grid and the stage
City, still: cityWorldFrom and buildCity, the glass shader, edges, bands, beams, beacons, plate names, labels, fitting, orbit, pan and zoom, and the ?spacestats readout
Selection: picking, hover tips, spaceSelect, showInfo taken out of select(), lit beams, rings, the inspector card and the part in the address
Folder tower: towerWorldFrom, floors with their real contents, labels, brackets, the folder and pulled-floor cards, sliding floors, and flying between tower and city
Street: walking, collision, the map, the breadcrumb, the hover card, and flying between city and street
Layers and the skyline: several drawn views in one city, and a repository's folders as buildings
Finish: light mode, reduced motion, keyboard, screen sizes, context loss and the budgets measured (the switch itself was shown on 2026-11-15, after step 6)
Records: every .dev file reconciled with the code, the README's Cyberspace paragraph, and the acceptance numbers worked out again

outOfScope: VR and XR, multiplayer, and editing .dev files (limitation no-edit)
Keeping camera positions anywhere but the address
Browser tests in CI: the repository has no npm dependencies, and adding them is a decision of its own

origin.description: Plan how to incorporate the new design for the 3D view.

entities.details: Done on 2026-11-15, when step 8 reconciled the .dev files with the code, added Cyberspace to the README and ran the spec's acceptance checklist again in Chrome with the numbers of the day. Two things are left, and neither is this plan's: the checklist in Safari and Firefox, which waits on decision cross-browser-checks (backlog item safari-firefox-checks), and standing a file's use cases side by side, which waits on decision per-entity-cities (backlog item side-by-side-entities). The branch perf/400-parts is still there for the owner to delete. Cyberspace's new look is plan cyberspace-gibson's.

entities.title: Give Cyberspace the Gibson look
entities.summary: Four pull requests after a design pass: the dark and the palette, the floor's traces, the towers' faces, then the arcs, labels and HUD.
entities.goal: Cyberspace looks as artboards 11 to 15 draw it and docs/cyberspace-mode-spec.md says, in dark mode (and by day in light mode, decision theme-switch), within the budgets of quality requirement space-frame-rate.
entities.approach: A design pass first, approved by the owner before any build: artboards 11 to 15, rendered with three.js core from this repository's data by a scratch prototype that also measured the budgets, and the spec's Rendering, Labels and HUD rewritten to match. Then one pull request per step, into main, in order, each from the latest main, each leaving the page working and checked as plan cyberspace-mode's steps were: the diff against the spec, the tests and both validators on a clean checkout, the page in a real browser beside the renders, the flat page's regression list and the ?spacestats readout. Merging deploys to cyberspace-explorer.com, so each merges only on the owner's word. A sub-session builds each step, one at a time, because every step changes index.html.

steps.title: Design pass: artboards 11 to 15, the spec's Rendering, Labels and HUD, decision space-gibson-look and this plan

G1 · Dark and palette: html.space and the dark block, Cyberspace's tokens, the sky and the glossy floor, fog, the glass's new colours, glowing edges, magenta beacons, multisampling below pixel ratio 2 only, the HUD's colours, and ?spacestats reading a pixel back

G2 · Floor traces: dagre's points kept, routeTraces, skylineTraces and traceAt with their tests, traces and pads in place of the quiet beams, picking on the floor, the map's traces, cityCalls counted again
G3 · Faces: faceText and its kin with their tests, the atlas and the codes, the glass shader's faces, the folder tower's floors and the skyline's buildings carrying their text, the reflections
G4 · Arcs, labels and HUD: lit beams as arcs, the labels' look and the street's rule for near towers, the legend and its icons, the words, the records and the acceptance checklist again

outOfScope: Turning the view toward what is selected: built in a pull request of its own, alongside
Motion of its own: glows that pulse, text that scrolls

origin.description: Make Cyberspace always dark, styled like the Gibson in Hackers, with a design pass approved before any build.
